_about: Companion data for docs/research/foreign-fx-map.md. 'integra_params' are MFX Parameter numbers n (1-32) of the PCM Synth Tone MFX block, taken from Roland INTEGRA-7 Editor model_excmap_mfx.js leaf order minus the four CTRL_ASGN leaves. 'jv_prm' is EFX Parameter n (Patch Common 00 0D + n - 1), from the JV-1010 Owner's Manual MIDI Implementation, 'Correspondence of the EFX algorithm and Exclusive Address'. JV raw type r = XV MFX type r + 1 by name and parameter list. Roland's own JV->XV conversions (https://github.com/sigma/integral/issues/206, map-check-roland-pairs.md) confirm the type numbering and show that XV types 1-40 store the JV EFX parameters verbatim: XV MFX Parameter n = JV EFX Parameter n, same raw value, Parameters 13-32 = 0. An XV Patch with MFX type 1-40 therefore converts with these same rows (jv_prm = XV Parameter n). 'roland_pairs' gives the evidence per type; 'confidence' grades the JV/XV source side (type and raw parameter identity). The Integra side (integra_params, conv) cannot be checked from the pairs and keeps the grades in foreign-fx-map.md. The XV 41-90 encoding is still unverified. XV 41-90 'copy_slots': XV MFX Parameter n lands on Integra MFX Parameter copy_slots[n-1]; the other Integra Parameters keep the target type's defaults. Listed only for types the corpus check (xv-mfx-fit-check.py) and the XV-5050 manual both support (foreign-fx-map.md, Unresolved 1); every other XV 41-90 type gets the target type's defaults.

conversions.drop: no Integra equivalent: list in the Conversion report. A drop row's 'neutral' is the value that loses nothing (centre pan): the converter reports the parameter only when it differs.
conversions.eq_hi_jv: JV 0-1 (4000/8000 Hz) -> Integra list 2000/4000/8000: target = source + 1
conversions.rate_jv: <x> Rate (sync sw) = 0 (Hz); <x> Rate (Hz) stored = round(20 * jv_rate_hz(i)); jv_rate_hz: i 0-98 -> 0.05*(i+1); 99-118 -> 5.0+0.1*(i-99); 119-125 -> 7.0+0.5*(i-119). Exact: every JV rate is a multiple of 0.05 Hz.
conversions.rate_jv_plain: Integra rotor speed stored 1-200 = Hz*20 (no sync slot): target = round(20 * jv_rate_hz(i)). Exact.
conversions.step_rate_jv: Integra Step Rate (Hz) stored 1-200 = Hz*10 (0.10-20.00 Hz): target = max(1, round(10 * jv_rate_hz(i))), sync sw = 0. 0.05 Hz clamps to 0.10 Hz; x.x5 Hz values round. JV note settings: unresolved.
conversions.delay500_jv: Delay (sync sw) = 0 (msec); msec = round(jv_delay500_ms(i)); jv_delay500_ms: i 0-49 -> 0.1*i; 50-59 -> 5.0+0.5*(i-50); 60-89 -> 10+(i-60); 90-115 -> 40+10*(i-90); 116-126 -> 300+20*(i-116). Values below 10 ms lose their sub-millisecond part.
conversions.delay1000_jv: i 0-115: sync sw = 0, msec = 200+5*i (i<70) or 550+10*(i-70). i 116-125: note (sync sw = 1), assumed order = XV note list *1 (1/16, 1/8T, 1/16., 1/8, 1/4T, 1/8., 1/4, 1/2T, 1/4., 1/2) -> Integra NOTE index 6+(i-116). Note order unverified.
conversions.post_gain: JV x1/x2/x4/x8 (0-3) = 0/+6/+12/+18 dB -> Integra Post Gain 0-18 dB: target = 6*i. Exact.
conversions.sustain_to_threshold: different control law (JV Sustain vs Integra Threshold): no formula. Leave Integra init and report.
conversions.phaser_manual_jv: JV Manual is a Hz table (i 0-19: 100+10*i; 20-54: 300+20*(i-20); 55-125: 1000+100*(i-55)); Integra Manual 0-127 has no published Hz curve: approximate and report.
conversions.level_balance: JV Level Balance A100:0B..A0:100B (0-100): Pitch1 Level = round(127*min(1,(100-x)/50)), Pitch2 Level = round(127*min(1,x/50)). Hypothesis (crossfade law not published).

params.roland_pairs: Roland copies JV raw 0/1 unchanged into XV Parameter 3 (1,790 Patches), while this row adds 1. XV-native Patches use 0-2 here (21 use 2), so the XV list has three entries. If the XV order is 2000/4000/8000 Hz like the Integra's, Roland's conversion lowers High Freq one step and this row is the parameter-faithful one; if not, the XV order differs from the Integra's and XV import needs its own rule. Unresolved; see map-check-roland-pairs.md.

classes.same: every source parameter copies raw; Integra-only parameters take the listed neutral value
classes.rescaled: same algorithm; every source parameter lands, some through a listed formula
classes.rescaled-lossy: same algorithm; some source parameters have no target (dropped or clamped) and go to the Conversion report
classes.substitute: different algorithm; closest Integra type, approximate
classes.none: no Integra MFX type; MFX goes to THRU and the effect goes to the Conversion report

roland_pairs_sends_and_patch_effects.efx_sends: JV EFX Chorus/Reverb Send (00 1B/00 1C) -> XV MFX Chorus/Reverb Send (00 02/00 03): identical in all 2,506 R02 Patches. Confirms the 'same' class of the send rows.
roland_pairs_sends_and_patch_effects.efx_mix_out: JV EFX Mix Out Send Level (00 1A) -> XV MFX Dry Send Level (00 01): identical in 2,506/2,506 R02 Patches. On the Integra 00 01 is a reserve, so the loss stands.
roland_pairs_sends_and_patch_effects.patch_chorus: JV Patch Chorus -> XV Chorus Type 1 CHORUS in 2,506/2,506 R02 Patches: Level and Output Select copy; Chorus Parameters 1-4 = JV Rate, Depth, Pre-Delay, Feedback raw (Rate and Pre-Delay 127 clamp to 125: 11 and 15 Patches); Parameters 5-8 fixed at 0, 7, 90, 0. Roland treats the JV chorus as the XV CHORUS type, not as a GM2 chorus.
roland_pairs_sends_and_patch_effects.patch_reverb: JV Patch Reverb -> XV Reverb Type 1 REVERB in 2,506/2,506 R02 Patches: Level copies; Reverb Parameter 1 = JV Reverb Type (ROOM1..PAN-DLY, 0-7), Parameters 2-4 = JV Time, HF Damp, Delay Feedback raw. XV REVERB type 1 is the JV reverb.
roland_pairs_sends_and_patch_effects.efx_control: EFX Control Source/Depth -> MFX Control: see jv-xv-roland-pairs.md (SYS-CTRL1 -> 99, SYS-CTRL2 -> 100, depth +1).
